- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct downward quickly — overcorrecting or lagging in mean reversion.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, particularly when recent history shows downward momentum.
- Forecast accuracy improves when model adjusts downward after a sharp rise, but often lags by 1–3 days.
- Model underestimates prices during prolonged downward trends, especially when true outcome shows resilience or mean reversion.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility — forecasts spike too high after minor price movements, then fails to recover.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture the true mean reversion pattern — tends to hold too high or too low relative to historical average.
- Model underestimates the impact of policy or market events (e.g., EU ETS auction changes) — often misses downward corrections or delays upward adjustments.
- Model shows strong bias toward recent high prices — fails to discount the influence of prior peaks unless explicitly modeled.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility — underestimates sharp drops or overestimates gradual declines.
